title: Good aside from loading time and extortionate premium
body: Simple, effective, satisfying, when the UI loads. It frequently does not load, stuck in that little loader animation despite several app restarts. -1 for this. The premium for long term use also prices me out - *at least* double what the value proposition is worth - it's a simple habit tracker with reminders and mindset orientation. There are free apps that do this with slightly less satisfying animations. -2.
author: cayhiew

title: How do ruin your brand overnight
body: I’ve been a long time fan of James Clear from his early days and seen him implement various monetisation methods but honestly never expected this day to come where he has clearly lost touch with his core audience of people wanting to improve themselves. No matter how good this app may or may not be, it’s pricing is beyond absurd. Furthermore, there is simply no justification for it being subscription based other than being a self serving method to hold your data to ransom should you ever contemplate leaving. One habit you don’t want to form is being dependent on this app. You simply don’t need it. James is simply trying to cash in on vulnerable people who are so gullible they believe the app is necessary for their improvement journey to be successful. For all his moral posturing, James has proven to be just another hypocrit selling himself out at the alter of the almighty dollar. Sad.
author: ramst3r

title: Needs refinements
body:
Nice idea but the app has a lot of basic issues.

Every time you complete a habit it takes you to another screen with a 10 second animation, so if you’ve just habit stacked and want to check off 4 habits you’re just sitting there waiting for a minute everytime. 

Riddled with a ton of small things like that.
author: itsleotheceo

title: Insanely expensive
body:
I started to use this app, and really like the look and functionality. However, when I looked into how much it was going to cost after the free trial, I was absolutely shocked to find that it was $200 AUD a year, or $25 AUD a month. 
My understanding of what’s included is that you only get to track three habits for that price, compared to one for the free app. 
To me, that pricing is actually quite ridiculous, and especially for what you get. 
I’ve followed James Clear since I read the book, but he’s lost a supporter here - this isn’t about helping people, it’s just a money grab. 
I’ll go back to my pen and paper habit tracker on the fridge.

title: Exclusionary pricing.
body:
James it’s clear that your ideas and in turn this app will add great value to many people’s lives. Just not for literally millions of people around the world currently facing cost of living crises. I believe your team has seriously misjudged the price point for what the app has to offer. Look into headspace functionality, content availability and price vs Atoms. You have asked your subscribers to leave good reviews but in good faith I can’t support pricing so out of touch with the reality of people’s lives and with the values underpinning your messaging and the apps ultimate goal. I wish you all the best with the roll out. 

For those not able to afford the app, pen and paper cards work just fine! I used that after reading the chapter detailing the approach in atomic habits, a book you could rent at your local library for free :)

title: A habit tracker that will help you build lifelong habits!
body:
A fresh take on habit tracking that is grounded from the wisdom of ‘Atomic Habits’. Compared to traditional habit trackers, Atoms helps build lifelong habits by encouraging on tracking one habit at a time until mastery (ie. habit automaticity), as well as setting clear habit intentions that is grounded to your desired identity.

As a huge fan Atomic Habits, I’m optimistic and excited to build lifelong habits with the help of Atoms - and if you’re looking for the same, I’d encourage you to give it a shot!
